chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abu Sa'id, from Abu Hamza, who said:

We were a group in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He called for food that we had no prior experience of being so delicious and fragrant. We were served dates so clear and beautiful that we looked at our own faces in them. A man said, 'We will surely be questioned about this bounty with which we have been favored in the presence of the son of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is more generous and noble than to feed you food, make it palatable, and then question you about it. But He will question you about what He has favored upon you through Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).'
ai.seo_question: What is the primary basis for divine accountability according to Imam al-Sadiq: material sustenance or spiritual guidance?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the principle of *al-Ni'mah* (blessing) versus *al-Hisab* (accountability), asserting that Allah’s generosity precludes holding servants accountable for the mere consumption of sustenance. He redirects the focus of divine reckoning toward the spiritual privilege of recognizing and following the Prophet and his Ahl al-Bayt, which serves as the true source of favor. This distinction highlights the Shia theological emphasis on *Ma'rifah* (gnosis) of the Imams as the primary metric for reward, rather than material consumption alone.
